security_spec.violation_condition: When QEMU takes an external interrupt with xtvec.mode=11 (vector table mode) but fails to encode the major interrupt identity in mcause/scause bits 15:0 and the minor interrupt identity in bits XLEN-2:16, instead using the legacy exception code format
security_spec.summary: mcause/scause exception code field changes to hold Major[15:0] and Minor[XLEN-2:16] interrupt identities when xtvec.mode=11 for external interrupts; QEMU TCG trap delivery must conditionally pack both identities or guest interrupt dispatch breaks

findings.finding: Smivt (xtvec.mode=11) is explicitly NOT implemented. Mode values >= 2 are rejected with a LOG_UNIMP warning. Silently dropping the write (WARL behavior) is spec-compliant for reserved modes. No Smivt-related security vulnerability exists because the feature is not claimed.
Same as write_mtvec — Smivt mode=11 is rejected for stvec as well. No Ssivt support exists.

scause is set in legacy format: cause code in bits 15:0, async flag in bit sxlen-1. Bits XLEN-2:16 are always zero. This is correct because Ssivt is not implemented — no minor/major interrupt identity encoding is required.

mcause is set in legacy format: cause code in bits 15:0, async flag in bit mxlen-1. Bits XLEN-2:16 are always zero. This is correct because Smivt is not implemented — no minor/major interrupt identity encoding is required.

stvec PC calculation only handles mode=0 (direct) and mode=1 (vectored). Mode=11 (Smivt interrupt vector table) would silently fall through to direct mode, but mode=11 is rejected by write_stvec, so this path is unreachable.
mtvec PC calculation only handles mode=0 (direct) and mode=1 (vectored). Mode=11 would silently fall through to direct mode, but mode=11 is rejected by write_mtvec, so this path is unreachable.

Future-implementation risk: if Smivt/Ssivt support is later added (allowing xtvec.mode=11 in write_mtvec/write_stvec and adding mivt/sivt/meivt/seivt CSRs), this function must also be updated to: (1) encode major interrupt identity in mcause/scause bits 15:0 and minor identity in bits XLEN-2:16 per the Smivt spec (§smivt, aclic.adoc:1275-1298); (2) use the interrupt vector table fetch from VTBASE+XLEN/8*vtoffset instead of the current mode-0/1 PC calculation. The current code has no guard that would prevent this omission — the mode check `(env->mtvec & 3) == 1` only matches mode=1, so mode=3 would silently fall through to direct mode with legacy cause encoding.

spec_citations.excerpt: mode 11: PC on Interrupt = M[VTBASE+XLEN/8*vtoffset] & VTMASK. If external interrupt: VTBASE = xeivt[XLEN-1:6]<<6, vtoffset = Minor Interrupt Identity (xtopei[26:16]). Else: VTBASE = xivt[XLEN-1:2]<<2, vtoffset = Major Interrupt Identity.
